claims.notes: [BATCH NOTE b076] Batch conventions for this document. (1) Anchoring: the sibling summary.json holds every cumulative and shell cell, so it is the least-writable artefact for §§1-4; ripley.csv anchors §5 (no JSON sibling carries the Ripley curve). (2) Method split: permutation p-values and permutation CI/envelope bounds carry per-value method 'recompute-script' per the batch brief, even though the recorded values also sit in the anchor file; recorded scalars that are not CI/p quantities (observed rates, null means, lift ratios, signal fractions, counts, parameters) carry 'read'. (3) Percentages quoted against fractions stored in summary.json use per-value arithmetic (100 * a) rather than a scale-bridging unit, to avoid a false hard mismatch. (4) Radii quoted in prose are anchored to the corresponding R_m / R_inner_m / R_outer_m cell rather than dropped as names.
